artifacts.body_markdown:
# DC-0001 — CanonPress Restructuring Through Meadows' Leverage Points

**This record is a schema test, not a migration.** The live artifact is still the
hand-authored React page; nothing here changes what renders today. It exists to
answer one question: *can the proposed artifact schema represent something
CanonPress has already published?*

It can, with one caveat recorded below.

## Drift found while modeling it

The shipped artifact disagrees with itself about its own ID:

- `layout.tsx` metadata: **`DC-001`** (three digits)
- page body, rendered: **`DC-0001`** (four digits)
- URL path: `/canonpress/deepcut/dc-001`
- `PRO-CANONPRESS-ARCH-001 [A]`: `DC-XXXX` — four digits

`artifact_id` above uses the canon-conformant four-digit form. The three-digit
URL is preserved in `source` rather than reconciled, because the URL is live and
renaming it here would hide the drift rather than fix it.

## Why this one was chosen for the test

It is the largest shipped artifact (12,413 bytes of JSX) and the output of
CanonPress Week 01 — the March cycle whose tuning log records
`status: COMPLETE`, nominated material *The Twelve Leverage Points to Intervene
in a System* (Donella Meadows). If the schema could not hold this, it could not
hold CanonPress's flagship work.

artifacts.body_markdown:
# GT-002 — The Outfit Doesn't Kill the Idea

*"On almost discarding a real idea because of the skin someone else put on it."*

**Deliberately modeled with its real three-digit ID, not canonicalised.**

`PRO-CANONPRESS-ARCH-001 [A]` specifies `GT-XXXX` — four digits. This artifact
ships as `GT-002`. I could have written `GT-0002` here and produced a clean
record; instead the record carries what is actually live, so
`canonpress.py validate` reports the drift as a warning rather than the schema
quietly absorbing it.

That is the whole reason this record exists in this form: **a validator that only
ever sees conformant input has never been tested.** Modeling the non-conformant
shipped artifact is what proves the check fires.

## What this artifact is, for the reboot's purposes

GROUNDTRUTH is defined in canon as *"Operator observation. Direct account of
lived experience... Capture raw signal before abstraction or interpretation
layers are applied."* This is that: a first-person account of nearly throwing
away a good idea because of how it was packaged.

It matters to the reboot because it is the series with the **lowest** production
cost — Operator-authored narrative, no council cycle, no synthesis — and it still
only produced two shipped artifacts. That is evidence the bottleneck is the
hand-authored React page, not the editorial pipeline above it.
